subject: Bridge commit / tier split and rate-card review for renewal
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@optimaretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@optimaretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal options — midterm uplift / bridge commit question

Hi Rachel,

We're kicking off our renewal planning for November and I need a clearer sense of how Redwood would handle a midterm uplift vs a bridge (short-term) commit. Two things specifically:

- If we add GPUs mid-contract, how do you split billing between the original reserved pool and the top-up? Is there proration or separate line items?
- We may want a 3-month bridge to cover Black Friday traffic; what discount tiers apply for short-term commits vs annual reserved?

Can you send a simple comparison (pricing + SLA/throughput guarantees) and any sample amendment language we can circulate with procurement? We're also interested in any credits you provide if throughput falls below the SLA during a scale event.

Thanks — Maria
Maria Lopez
CFO, Optima Retail

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@optimaretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — midterm uplift / bridge commit question

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary below and I attached a compact comparison + amendment draft for procurement.

Short answers up front:
- Midterm uplift (extend reserved commit): we pro-rate the incremental capacity for the remainder of the term and then roll the new baseline into the next renewal price if you choose to keep it. Pricing tilts toward the annual rate once you commit for >6 months.
- Bridge commits (1–3 months): billed as time-limited reserved capacity at a higher per-GPU rate than annual (reflects capacity reservation cost) with smaller discounts; can be combined with burst-backed routing to avoid over-provisioning.
- SLA credits: we offer SLA credits for sustained throughput below the agreed guarantee (threshold and measurement window listed in the draft). Short bridge commits have a modified SLA credit schedule (shorter windows).

Attachments: OPTI-374_renewal_options_2026-08-19.pdf (comparison table + numbers) and OPTI-374_amendment_draft_2026-08-19.docx (procurement-friendly amendment).

Questions for you so we tailor numbers:
1) Expected Black Friday baseline vs peak (avg tokens/sec or QPS) and estimated weeks of elevated demand?
2) Do you prefer a single pooled approach (one reserve that scales) or separate line items for the bridge? Procurement often prefers separate line items for easier rollback.

I'll pull a quick priced example once you confirm peak weeks and preference.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — midterm uplift / bridge commit question

Adding a few technical/ops clarifications to feed into the amendment language:

- Billing model: incremental GPUs added mid-term are invoiced pro-rata from the date the capacity is enabled. We keep the upfront commit amortized across the remaining months; the new baseline only locks in if they sign a term extension.
- Throttling & routing: for bridge commits we recommend pairing with burst routing to fail over to lower-cost hosted variants if internal pool is saturated — reduces need for very large bridge commits while maintaining availability.
- Measurement: throughput guarantee measured as 95th pct token throughput over a sliding 30-day window (unless customer requests stricter window). Credits are a percentage of that month's committed spend.

I updated the amendment draft with a short paragraph on measurement and routing; see Ben for exact dollar credit tiers.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@optimaretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T14:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — midterm uplift / bridge commit question

Thanks Rachel and Karthik — useful. A couple of constraints from procurement:

- They want bridge commits as separate lines so they can avoid an automatic rollover into next year's baseline.
- Any credit calculation needs to be formulaic and auditable — procurement wants the exact SLA measurement window called out.

For numbers: Black Friday prep window is 6 weeks (2/9–3/22) — apologies for odd dates, our calendar is fiscal shifted. Baseline token throughput today ~1.2M tokens/day, expected peak ~4.8M tokens/day during the 6-week window.

Can you provide an example quote: 3-month bridge for +16 GPUs vs a midterm uplift to add +8 GPUs permanently (restick into renewal)? If you could show monthly line items and total cost per model of throughput (simple $/1M tokens estimate) that would be ideal.

Maria
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@optimaretail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — midterm uplift / bridge commit question

Hi Maria — attaching the priced examples inline and the draft amendment (attached). Summary:

Option A — 3-month bridge (16 GPUs):
- Rate: $5,400 / GPU / month (bridge rate)
- Total (3 months): $259,200
- Effective $/1M tokens (peak) ~ $1,080 (model and perf dependent)
- SLA: modified window; credits tiered at 5%/10%/20% for SLA misses (30/60/90-day sustained below threshold)

Option B — Midterm uplift to add +8 GPUs (pro-rated remainder of term, converts to baseline on renewal if chosen):
- Incremental pro-rate (remaining 15 months): $3,200 / GPU / month equivalent -> pro-rated charge for remainder = $153,600 total now, then included in renewal pricing if they keep it
- Effective $/1M tokens (amortized) ~ $640

Notes: Bridge gives immediate headroom but is ~1.7x the per-GPU cost vs midterm uplift amortized; procurement wins clarity with separate line items. We can offer a one-time 5% credit if they sign both the midterm uplift and the bridge together (bundled commitment incentive).

Attachments: OPTI-374_renewal_options_2026-08-19.pdf (contains the above tables) and OPTI-374_amendment_draft_2026-08-19.docx

If procurement needs more explicit audit language around measurement we'll add a formula appendix (I can draft).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
